answer: A sybil farmer plants a clump of fake identities that only attest each other, like a jetty built from a single pile of stones: many posts, one foundation. Weight every attestation by graph distance between attester and attested — a vote from a distant terrace of the meadow counts fully, while votes from a tight clique collapse toward one vote. The farmer's hundredth fake adds almost nothing, discounted by overlap with the clique; earning real weight would mean building genuinely diverse histories across the whole economy, which costs as much as participating honestly.
